title: Study stock data
intro: Tools for exploring past data while you learn. They do not tell you which stock is better.
tabs.label: Study tools

scr.title: Stock screener
scr.desc: Filter stocks by P/E, dividend yield and market cap. Leave a field blank to skip it. Results are sorted by ticker A–Z; click a column header to change the order.
scr.col.name: Company
scr.invalidNumber: Enter a number of 0 or more
scr.note: Stocks without a P/E or dividend are left out when you filter by that value · OTC and delisted stocks are not included
cmp.title: Compare 2–4 stocks
cmp.desc: See how the split-adjusted close changed, in %, with every line starting at 0% on the first day of the range.
cmp.hoverHint: Hover or tap the chart to see each day's values
cmp.formula: % = (adjusted close ÷ close on the first day of the range − 1) × 100
exp.title: Download price history (CSV)
exp.desc: Daily prices of one stock for the date range above. Opens in Excel and includes a source line and a disclaimer.
bt.title: DCA vs lump sum backtest
bt.desc: Using past prices, see how today's value differs between investing the same amount every month (DCA) and investing the total at once in the first month.
bt.proOnly: This feature is for Pro members
bt.upgrade: See Pro membership on your account page
bt.method.title: How it is calculated
bt.method.1: Buys at the split-adjusted close on the first trading day of each month
bt.method.2: DCA invests the amount you entered every month · Lump sum invests the full total on the first trading day of the start month
bt.method.3: No fees, no dividends, and share amounts are not rounded
bt.method.4: Final value uses the close of the latest closed session · Difference = rounded DCA value − rounded lump-sum value
bt.note: This uses past data for learning only. It does not predict future results and does not say which approach suits anyone.
hist.title: Compare and backtest history
hist.desc: The latest 20 items are kept. Click an item to reopen its page with the same values.
hist.empty: No history yet. Try a comparison or a DCA backtest first.
